places.order: Cappuccino in the courtyard; cake slice; weekend brunch (see note)
places.notes: Source: newinzurich.com brunch page + zueriplausch.ch / Yelp hours
places.famousFor: Hidden inner courtyard with a fountain a minute from Paradeplatz; professional baristas, cakes and a big weekend brunch spread
places.goodToKnow: Mon-Fri 06:30-22:00, Sat 08:00-22:00, Sun 10:00-18:00. Weekend brunch ~CHF 58 pp includes champagne - ask for it without; à-la-carte coffee & cake is the easy option

places.name: JUNi Kaffeefenster Paradeplatz

places.order: Flat white; matcha latte; a pastry
places.notes: Source: newinzurich.com guide + NZZ / juni-zurich.ch

places.goodToKnow: Open daily (check exact times); standing/takeaway only - drink it on the square between Sprüngli and the banks

places.name: The Monocle Shop & Café
places.cuisine: Specialty coffee / light bites / magazine shop
places.near: Tram 2/4 to Feldeggstrasse or Höschgasse, 2-min walk
places.order: Cappuccino or flat white; cake or a light bite
places.notes: Source: newinzurich.com guide + monocle.com / local.ch hours
places.famousFor: Monocle magazine's Zürich outpost: high-quality coffee, newspapers and an adjoining design boutique - a stylish Seefeld pause
places.goodToKnow: Open daily; Sun from 08:00 (closing reported 19:00-22:00 depending on source). Small, cosy; good after the lake promenade

places.name: ētre patisserie

places.order: Seasonal tart or entremet; croissant; coffee
places.notes: Source: newinzurich.com guide + corner.inc / Apple Maps hours
places.famousFor: Photogenic French-inspired patisserie in Seefeld praised by pastry bloggers; tarts, entremets and croissants at a very high level
places.goodToKnow: Sun 09:00-15:00 (open Sundays); small space, pastries sell out - come before noon

places.name: Schwarzenbach Kaffeebar & Teecafé
places.cuisine: Coffee roastery espresso bar / tea café

places.notes: Source: schwarzenbach.ch contact page via search + zuerich.com
places.famousFor: Family delicatessen since 1864 (5th generation) roasting its own coffee in the Old Town; espresso bar beside the colonial-goods shop and a tea café across the lane - a true Zürich original
places.goodToKnow: Mon-Fri 09:00-18:30, Sat 09:00-17:00, Sun CLOSED

places.name: Le Hall - Baur au Lac
places.near: 5-min walk from Paradeplatz or Bürkliplatz
places.order: Morning coffee with a patisserie dessert; Afternoon Tea (Länggass teas, finger sandwiches, scones, clotted cream)
places.notes: Source: bauraulac.ch Le Hall + afternoon-tea pages
places.famousFor: The lobby lounge of Zürich's grand family-owned hotel (since 1844), 'the most beautiful living room in the city'; open to non-guests for morning coffee, in-house patisserie desserts and a British afternoon tea
places.goodToKnow: Mon-Fri 08:30-23:00, Sat-Sun 09:00-23:00. Afternoon Tea served Oct-Mar daily 13:30-17:00 - book ahead (+41 44 220 50 64). Smart-casual; pricey. The Pavillon restaurant is closed for renovation

places.name: Latte Stories
places.cuisine: Specialty coffee / brunch / kids play café
places.near: S-Bahn/tram to Oerlikon, then bus/tram along Hagenholzstrasse (near Messe/Hallenstadion)
places.order: Flat white for parents; weekend brunch plates; kids' menu
places.notes: Source: kidzh.ch review + corner.inc hours + lattestories.ch
places.famousFor: Purpose-built family café: indoor play corner plus an outdoor playground in full view of the tables, stroller-friendly layout, high chairs and changing table; coffee roasted by the owners
places.goodToKnow: Mon-Fri 07:30-17:00, Sat-Sun 08:00-17:00 (open Sunday); weekend brunch 08:00-14:00. Best kid-friendly café in the city for a family of 7

places.name: Wim Bakery
places.near: Tram 4/13 to Wipkingerplatz or Röschibachstrasse, short walk
places.order: Cinnamon roll; sourdough slice with butter; coffee
places.notes: Source: zuerich.com Wim Bakery page + zuri.net hours
places.famousFor: Neighbourhood sourdough bakery with an open bakehouse you can watch, marble tables and excellent cinnamon rolls; a pleasant walk along the Limmat from Kreis 5
places.goodToKnow: Wed-Sun 08:00-16:00 (open Sunday), closed Mon-Tue. Pastries sell out by early afternoon

places.name: Kafi Dihei
places.near: Tram 9/14 to Zurlindenstrasse or Zwinglihaus
places.order: Cake of the day with coffee; weekend brunch plate
places.notes: Source: kafidihei.ch via search + zuerich.com
places.famousFor: 'Coffee at home' - a feel-good neighbourhood café with homemade cakes, snacks and a relaxed weekend brunch; regularly on Zürich best-brunch lists
places.goodToKnow: Mon, Wed-Fri 08:30-18:00; Sat-Sun 09:00-18:00 (open Sunday); Tue closed. No reservations even for large groups - arrive early with 7

places.name: Zoo Zürich
places.near: Zurichbergstrasse 221; tram 6 from the main station to Zoo terminus
places.order: The immersive Masoala Rainforest hall and the elephant park
places.notes: Saved POI
places.famousFor: Zoo Zurich, famous for its Masoala Rainforest and Kaeng Krachan elephant park
places.goodToKnow: Open daily year-round, from 9:00 (closes earlier in winter).

places.name: UBS Polybahn
places.near: Lower station at Central, Zurich, by the Limmat; tram/bus hub right outside.
places.order: Ride the short funicular up to the Polyterrasse for the classic viewpoint over Zurich's old town.
places.notes: Saved POI
places.famousFor: UBS Polybahn, Zurich's historic funicular climbing from Central up to the ETH/Polyterrasse with city and lake views.
places.goodToKnow: Runs frequently on weekdays/Sat (limited Sundays); ~100 m climb in about a minute; cheap fare, Swiss travel passes accepted.

places.name: FIFA Museum
places.near: Seestrasse 27, opposite Bahnhof Enge; tram 5/7/8/13 or S-Bahn to Bahnhof Enge
places.order: See the FIFA World Cup trophy gallery and play the interactive football skills games
places.notes: Saved POI
places.famousFor: FIFA World Football Museum — interactive football museum on three floors with trophies, memorabilia and the original FIFA World Cup history
places.goodToKnow: Open Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, closed Mon; adult ~CHF 26, under 7 free; free with Swiss Travel Pass/Zürich Card; allow 2-3 hrs

places.name: Hürlimannbad & Spa Zurich
places.near: Brandschenkestrasse 150, central Zurich (Enge/Aussersihl); short tram ride from the center
places.order: Soak in the 35C rooftop infinity pool with city/Alps views; try the emerald bath and the Roman-Irish ritual
places.notes: From Saved POI · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Thermal spa inside the historic stone vaults of the former Hurlimann brewery, famed for its rooftop infinity pool
places.goodToKnow: Paid admission incl. towel/robe; book ahead; adults-focused; rooftop pool open year-round

places.name: Botanical Garden
places.near: Zürich city, near Hottingen; tram/bus to the garden
places.order: The tropical, savanna and mountain-forest greenhouse domes
places.notes: From Saved POI · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: University of Zürich botanical garden known for its three modern semi-spherical glass greenhouse domes and themed plant collections
places.goodToKnow: Free entry to the park; greenhouses have set opening hours

places.name: Kunsthaus Zürich
places.near: Trams 3, 8 or 9 (or bus 31) to 'Kunsthaus' stop; walkable from the main station
places.order: Collection ticket (CHF 24) or the 'All in One' ticket (CHF 36) covering all exhibitions; don't miss the Giacometti and Munch holdings and the Bührle collection in the new wing
places.notes: Zurich's flagship art museum and a top cultural pick; excellent for a half-day visit · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Switzerland's largest art collection — Munch, Giacometti, Swiss and modern masters, plus a major 2021 Chipperfield extension
places.goodToKnow: Open Tue–Wed & Fri–Sun 10:00–18:00, Thu until 20:00, closed Mondays. Free admission to the collection and small exhibitions on Wednesdays. Book major exhibitions online in advance

places.name: Swiss National Museum
places.near: Right next to Zürich Hauptbahnhof (Central Station); tram/bus to Central, Bahnhofstrasse/HB or Sihlquai/HB
places.order: Permanent exhibition on Swiss history and identity; the striking building and courtyard themselves; check current temporary exhibitions
places.notes: Iconic castle-like landmark right by the station — ideal first stop · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Fairy-tale castle-like building housing Switzerland's largest collection of cultural-history artefacts, telling the story of the country from prehistory to today
places.goodToKnow: Open Tue–Sun 10:00–17:00, Thu until 19:00, closed Mondays. Covered by Zürich Card; 10% discount with SBB RailAway combi. Family-friendly and centrally located

places.name: Museum Rietberg
places.near: Tram 7 to 'Museum Rietberg' stop; set within the 17-acre Rieterpark
places.order: Special-exhibition ticket (CHF 18); explore the Asian and African collections, then stroll the surrounding Rieterpark
places.notes: A tranquil, distinctive museum in a beautiful park setting — a change of pace from the city-center museums · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: The only museum in Switzerland dedicated to non-European art — internationally renowned collections from Asia, Africa, the Americas and Oceania, set in a leafy park
places.goodToKnow: Open Tue, Wed, Sat, Sun 10:00–17:00 and Thu 10:00–20:00 (check for Friday/Monday closures). Open holidays 10:00–17:00 except closed Dec 25. Accepts Zürich Card and Swiss Museum Pass. Combine with a park walk

places.name: Natural History Museum of the University of Zurich
places.near: In the main University of Zurich building, city center; tram 6/9/10 to ETH/Universitätsspital, or Polybahn from Central
places.order: Free entry (donation appreciated via cash or TWINT at exit); see the zoological dioramas, dinosaur/fossil skeletons and the popular animal exhibits
places.notes: One of Zurich's best free attractions; the former Zoological Museum now sits under the merged Natural History Museum of UZH · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Free natural-history collections — zoology, palaeontology, anthropology and botany — merged in 2024 into one university museum; famous for its animal dioramas and fossils
places.goodToKnow: Open Tue–Sun 10:00–17:00, Thu until 20:00 (closed Thu 17:00–17:30), closed Mondays. Admission is FREE — excellent for families and rainy days. Some basement-gallery closures scheduled in spring 2026 (open normally on weekends)

places.name: Pavillon Le Corbusier
places.area: Zürich (Kreis 8), Seefeld — Zürichhorn park by the lake
places.near: Tram 2 or 4 to 'Höschgasse', short walk to the lakeside pavilion at Zürichhorn
places.order: Admission (CHF 15) to tour the interior and design exhibitions; the vivid enamel-panel facade is the standout photo subject
places.notes: An Instagrammable architectural gem; verify it's within the open season before visiting · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: The last building Le Corbusier designed and his only one in steel and glass — a colorful, highly photogenic modernist pavilion by the lake
places.goodToKnow: SEASONAL — 2026 season runs 17 April–29 November only. Open daily 12:00–18:00, Thu until 20:00. Free on Thursdays after 17:00 and with Zürich Card. No online tickets (buy on site). Great for architecture-photography fans

places.name: Cabaret Voltaire
places.near: In the Niederdorf old town, walkable from the main station; near tram stops at Central / Rathaus
places.order: See the Dada exhibition in the historic rooms and vaulted cellar; browse the Dada shop; catch a soirée or temporary show in the Historical Hall
places.notes: An atmospheric hidden gem for anyone interested in art history and the avant-garde; it doubles as a bar/café but is a genuine cultural/museum site · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: The 1916 birthplace of the Dada art movement — now a museum, cultural space, café and shop dedicated to Dada history and contemporary art
places.goodToKnow: Open Tue–Thu 17:00–23:00, Fri–Sat 13:30–00:30, Sun 13:30–18:00, closed Mondays. A hidden-gem stop; hours skew afternoon/evening, so plan around them. Small venue — great for art-history lovers

places.name: Museum of Design Zurich
places.near: Ausstellungsstrasse 60 is near the main station/Zürich-West; trams to Museum für Gestaltung / Toni-Areal in Zürich-West
places.order: Regular ticket (CHF 15) or combined ticket for all locations (CHF 20); see rotating design/graphic exhibitions at Ausstellungsstrasse and the collection displays at the Toni-Areal
places.notes: A must for design and graphic-arts enthusiasts; also operates the Pavillon Le Corbusier · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Switzerland's leading design and applied-arts museum, renowned for its poster, graphic-design and product-design collections
places.goodToKnow: Open Tue–Sun 10:00–17:00, Thu until 20:00, closed Mondays. Under-20s free; free every Thursday from 17:00. No online tickets (buy on site). Two sites — check which exhibition is where

places.name: Grossmünster
places.area: Altstadt (Old Town), right bank of the Limmat
places.near: 5-min walk from Zürich HB via Bahnhofstrasse and across the river; tram 4 or 15 to Helmhaus, then a short walk. On the right bank next to Rathausbrücke.
places.order: Church entry is free; climb the Karlsturm tower (187 steps) to a viewing platform with six panoramic windows for one of the best views over the Old Town and lake. Don't miss the crypt, Zwingli's pulpit, and the modern stained glass by Sigmar Polke and Augusto Giacometti.
places.notes: A must-see and the defining landmark of Zurich; verified open with active 2026 reviews despite ongoing renovation. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Zurich's iconic twin-towered Romanesque cathedral, cradle of the Swiss-German Reformation (Huldrych Zwingli preached here from 1519); its silhouette is the symbol of the city.
places.goodToKnow: Church open Mar–Oct 10:00–18:00 (closed Tue), Nov–Feb 10:00–17:00 (closed Tue); Karlsturm tower ~CHF 5, open ~10:00–17:00 (Apr–Oct) / to 16:30 (Nov–Mar), pay on site. NOTE: a renovation is underway 2026–2027 with scaffolding and some limited-access areas, but the church remains open. Tower stairs are steep and narrow — not ideal for those with mobility issues; fine for older children.

places.name: Fraumünster Church
places.area: Altstadt (Old Town), left bank at Münsterhof
places.near: Tram 4 or 15 to Helmhaus, or walk ~7 min from Zürich HB down Bahnhofstrasse to Paradeplatz, then to Münsterhof. Directly across the river from the Grossmünster.
places.order: Buy the entry ticket and take the audio-guide (~45 min) covering the Chagall and Giacometti windows, the church history and Reformation, and the crypt exhibition on over 1,200 years of city history. Best light on the choir windows is on a bright day.
places.notes: One of Zurich's top cultural attractions; verified open with Jun 2026 reviews. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Home to five monumental stained-glass windows (each ~10 m high) designed by Marc Chagall in 1970, plus a rose window by Chagall and a north-transept window by Augusto Giacometti — a highlight of 20th-century religious art.
places.goodToKnow: Generally open daily ~10:00–18:00; Mar–Oct closed to tourists on Sunday until after the morning service. Small admission fee. Photography of the Chagall windows is typically restricted — check on-site signage. Family-friendly; the audio-guide keeps kids engaged.

places.name: Lindenhof
places.near: ~7-min walk from Zürich HB along the Limmat, then up. Easiest via the eastern staircase (~60 steps) from the river, or a gentler approach up Schlüsselgasse from St. Peter. Tram 6/7/11/13 to Rennweg, then a short walk.
places.order: Free to visit any time. Take in the viewpoint over the river and rooftops, relax under the lindens, and watch locals play the oversized outdoor chess games (near knee-high pieces). Great sunset spot.
places.notes: Selected as the quintessential free Old-Town viewpoint; verified with 2026 Tripadvisor reviews. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: A tranquil linden-shaded hilltop square — site of a 4th-century Roman fort and later a Carolingian palace — offering one of the best free panoramas over the Old Town, the Limmat, Grossmünster and the university.
places.goodToKnow: Open 24/7, no ticket. Go early morning or golden hour for photos and fewer crowds. Family- and stroller-friendly if you take the ramped/gentler routes rather than the staircase; benches and shade make it a good rest stop.

places.name: Steakhouse Old Town
places.area: Altstadt, right (east) bank of the Limmat
places.near: ~5–8 min walk from Zürich HB across the river; tram 4 or 15 to Rudolf-Brun-Brücke or Helmhaus puts you at either end of the quarter.
places.order: Wander Niederdorfstrasse (the longest lane in the Old Town) and its side alleys on foot; browse boutiques and antique dealers by day. Visit Cabaret Voltaire (museum/gallery). Combine with nearby Grossmünster and the riverside promenade.
places.notes: The essential Old-Town walking district; verified with 2026 Tripadvisor reviews. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: The atmospheric, car-free heart of the Old Town — locally 'Dörfli' — a maze of medieval cobblestone lanes, historic houses, cafés, independent shops and, on Spiegelgasse, Cabaret Voltaire, birthplace of the Dada art movement (1916).
places.goodToKnow: Free to explore; the quarter is a pedestrian zone. Lively and family-friendly by day; it turns into a busy nightlife hub after dark, so daytime suits families best. Wear comfortable shoes for the cobblestones.

places.name: St. Peter
places.area: Altstadt (Old Town), left bank at St. Peterhofstatt
places.near: ~7-min walk from Zürich HB; tram 6/7/11/13 to Rennweg, then a couple of minutes on foot up toward Lindenhof. Just above Weinplatz on the left bank.
places.order: Free entry — step inside the light Baroque nave (rebuilt 1706, the first church built under Protestant rule) and step out onto the quiet St. Peterhofstatt square to photograph the enormous clock face. Pairs naturally with the short climb up to Lindenhof.
places.notes: A compact, free Old-Town highlight famed for its record clock; verified with 2026 reviews. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: The oldest parish church in Zurich (foundations pre-900), crowned by the largest church clock face in Europe — a tower dial about 8.7 m in diameter that was for centuries the city's official timekeeper.
places.goodToKnow: Free admission (donations welcome). Typical hours Mon–Fri ~08:00–18:00, Sat ~10:00–16:00, Sun ~noon–17:00 — verify on the day. The clock face is best photographed from St. Peterhofstatt square or across the river. The tower interior itself is generally not open to tourists.

places.name: Zürich's Town Hall
places.area: Altstadt (Old Town), right bank on Limmatquai at Rathausbrücke
places.near: Tram 4 or 15 to Rathaus stop on Limmatquai, right outside; ~6-min walk from Zürich HB across the river. Next to the Rathausbrücke pedestrian bridge.
places.order: Admire and photograph the ornate river façade from the Rathausbrücke or the opposite (left) bank. The interior with its historic council chambers can occasionally be seen on guided tours / open days — check the city site for scheduled visits.
places.notes: A distinctive riverside civic landmark; verified with Tripadvisor reviews and city tourism sources. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Zurich's late-Renaissance town hall (built 1694–1698), remarkable for rising straight out of the Limmat on piles driven into the riverbed, with arches anchored in the water — still the seat of the cantonal and city parliaments.
places.goodToKnow: Exterior viewing is free any time; it's a working government building, so interior access is limited to tours/events. The façade over the water photographs best from the left bank, especially in soft evening light. Combine with the adjacent Old Town and Grossmünster.

places.name: ZSG-Schifffahrt
places.near: Board at Bürkliplatz landing stage in the city centre; trams 2, 5, 8, 9, 11 stop at Bürkliplatz. Also boardable at Zürichhorn and other lakeside stages. ZVV/Swiss Travel Pass often valid on scheduled routes.
places.order: Take the short 'Kleine Rundfahrt' (~1h25) round trip to Zürichhorn and back (approx. CHF 9.40 in 2nd class), or the long 4h15 crossing to Rapperswil and back (approx. CHF 28 in 2nd class); themed cruises include the Breakfast/Late-Riser's Brunch boat, Fondue Cruise and Steamboat Dinner.
places.notes: Iconic and essential Zurich activity; ZSG is the official lake shipping company and confirmed operating in 2026. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Scenic scheduled boat cruises across Lake Zurich with views of the shoreline villas, hills and, on clear days, the Alps; the classic Zurich lake experience with over 1.5 million passengers a year.
places.goodToKnow: Summer timetable runs 3 April–18 October 2026 with peak-season (most departures) 1 May–30 September 2026; more limited service in winter. Tickets at the Bürkliplatz office or on board. Family-friendly; sit on the upper open deck for the best photos and Alps views. Book themed dinner/brunch cruises in advance.

places.name: Hotel UTO KULM car-free hideaway in Zurich
places.near: S10 S-Bahn from Zurich HB to Uetliberg (endpoint, ~20 min, every 30 min). NOTE: due to SZU tunnel construction the underground tracks 21/22 at Zurich HB are closed 29 April–18 October 2026, so the S10 runs only from Selnau (an 8-min walk from HB, or tram to Stauffacher).
places.order: Ride the S10 to the top, walk ~10 min to the summit, then climb the lookout tower (small fee ~CHF 2) for the 360° view; optionally hike the scenic Planet Trail (Planetenweg) ridge path toward Felsenegg (~2 hrs).
places.notes: Top-rated Zurich viewpoint, confirmed operating in 2026; plan around the temporary S10 rerouting from Selnau. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Zurich's 'house mountain' (869 m) with a panoramic observation tower giving sweeping views over the city, the whole length of Lake Zurich and the Alps on clear days.
places.goodToKnow: Go on a clear day for Alps views; sunset and autumn/winter 'above the fog' inversion days are spectacular. Family- and stroller-friendly path from the station. Uto Kulm hotel/restaurant with a large view terrace at the summit.

places.name: Restaurant Laufen Castle at the Rheinfalls
places.area: Neuhausen am Rheinfall / Schloss Laufen, near Schaffhausen (day trip from Zurich)
places.near: Train from Zurich HB to 'Schloss Laufen am Rheinfall' (about 50–60 min); the north bank at Neuhausen is reached via Schaffhausen. Boats operated by Rhyfall-Mändli run seasonally.
places.order: Take the boat 'rock ride' out to the central rock and climb its stairs to the mid-falls platform (~30 min round trip); combine with entry to Schloss Laufen (CHF 5, includes Historama and viewing platforms) and the riverside viewing decks. Summer-only short boat trip in the falls basin (surcharge ~CHF 12 adult / CHF 8 child).
places.notes: Verified real and freely accessible year-round; boat rides are seasonal. Excellent nature day trip from Zurich. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: The largest waterfall in Europe – roughly 150 m wide with water thundering 23 m down; a dramatic natural spectacle and a classic half-day trip from Zurich.
places.goodToKnow: The falls are freely accessible year-round; boat trips are seasonal (roughly spring–autumn, weather-dependent). Water is fullest and most powerful in early summer from snowmelt. Family-friendly. Best photos from the Känzeli platform below Schloss Laufen and from the boat.

places.name: Zürichhorn
places.near: Tram 2 or 4 to Höschgasse or Fröhlichstrasse, or ZSG lake boat to the Zürichhorn landing stage; also a pleasant ~30-min walk along the lake from Bürkliplatz.
places.order: Stroll the promenade from Bürkliplatz to Zürichhorn, watch Tinguely's 'Heureka' kinetic sculpture run (daily at 11:00, 15:00 and 19:00 for ~8 min in season), picnic on the lawns, and visit the adjacent Chinese Garden; a lake boat also stops here.
places.notes: Verified public park and promenade; a scenic, free way to combine walking, sculpture, swimming and the Chinese Garden. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: A relaxed lakeside park at the end of the eastern promenade, with landscaped meadows, sculptures (Jean Tinguely's kinetic 'Heureka', Henry Moore, Pavillon Le Corbusier nearby), swimming spots and the Chinese Garden.
places.goodToKnow: Free and open year-round; liveliest and greenest May–September. Family-friendly with playgrounds and lakeside eateries. 'Heureka' operates in the warmer season; time your visit to one of the three daily run times for the moving sculpture.

places.name: Chinagarten Zürich
places.near: Tram 2 or 4 to Höschgasse, then a short walk; or ZSG lake boat to Zürichhorn. On the eastern lakeside promenade beside Zürichhorn park.
places.order: Wander the ponds, pavilions and 'Three Friends of Winter' (pine, bamboo, plum) plantings; join a guided public tour (first Thursday of the month, April–October, 18:00–19:00, ~CHF 15 pp) for the symbolism.
places.notes: Verified and open in the 2026 season; a peaceful, photogenic stop at the end of the lakeside walk. Note reduced winter hours. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: An authentic large-scale Chinese temple garden on the lakeshore, a gift from Zurich's sister city Kunming (opened 1994); considered one of the most impressive Chinese gardens outside China.
places.goodToKnow: Seasonal opening: daily 11:00–19:00 April–October; reduced/closed in the coldest months (winter hours ~11:00–17:00). Modest entry fee (around CHF 4–5; some sources note free). Small and photogenic – best in spring blossom or autumn colour. Family-friendly.

places.name: Bürkliplatz
places.area: Zurich city centre (west lakeshore, at the lake outflow)
places.near: Trams 2, 5, 8, 9 and 11 stop at Bürkliplatz; central and walkable from Zurich HB (~15 min) via Bahnhofstrasse.
places.order: Walk the promenade for the Alps view, catch a ZSG lake cruise from here, browse the Saturday flea market (May–October, 230+ stalls) or the twice-weekly 'Bürklimäärt' vegetable market.
places.notes: Verified central lakeside square and promenade; the prime free viewpoint and boat hub in the city. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: The central lakefront square where Lake Zurich meets the city, offering the classic view down the lake to the Alps on clear days, plus the main boat terminal and a famous flea market.
places.goodToKnow: Free and open year-round; go on a clear day (or at sunset) for the best Alps-over-the-lake photos. Flea market is seasonal (Saturdays, May–October). Family-friendly; combine with a boat trip or the Bahnhofstrasse walk.

places.name: Seebad Enge
places.near: Tram 5 or 20 to Rentenanstalt, or a short walk along the western promenade from Bürkliplatz; on Mythenquai.
places.order: Swim in the open lake from the floating platforms or the 44 m lanes, relax on the deck; in the cooler season enjoy the lakeside sauna. There is also a women-only section.
places.notes: Verified seasonal lake bath with confirmed 2026 dates; one of Zurich's most scenic swimming spots. Open summer only. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: A photogenic wooden lake bath (Badi) built out over Lake Zurich with open-lake swimming, floating platforms and a much-loved lakeside sauna, plus city-and-lake views.
places.goodToKnow: Summer-only: 2026 bathing season runs 9 May–20 September; core hours roughly 08:00–20:00 in peak summer (opens 09:00 early/late season, weather-dependent but open mornings in any weather). Small entry fee. Very photogenic at sunset; can be busy on hot days.

places.name: Frauenbad Stadthausquai
places.area: Zurich city centre (on the Limmat, off the lake)
places.near: Central, walkable from Bürkliplatz/Bahnhofstrasse; nearby trams to Helmhaus/Bürkliplatz. On Stadthausquai on the Limmat just below the lake.
places.order: Swim in the two 30 m+ pools on the river with a city backdrop (women only during the day); in the evening the venue becomes the 'Barfussbar' (Barefoot Bar), which is also open to men.
places.notes: Verified historic women's lake bath, operating in the summer season; the evening Barfussbar is a well-known relaxed (non-alcohol-focused) riverside spot. Open summer only. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: A beautiful Art Nouveau open-air bathing pavilion from 1888 on the Limmat, a women-only day-time bath and one of the city's most photogenic historic Badis.
places.goodToKnow: Summer-only, roughly mid-May to mid-September (weather-dependent). Women only in the daytime; the evening Barfussbar admits everyone. Historic, architecturally striking and very central. Small entry fee.

places.name: Luftseilbahn Adliswil-Felsenegg
places.near: S4 train from Zurich HB to Adliswil (~15–20 min), then a short walk/bus to the valley station; total ~30 min from HB. Cable car fare is inexpensive and ZVV-integrated.
places.order: Ride the cable car up, enjoy the Felsenegg viewpoint terrace, then walk the panoramic 'Planet Trail' (Planetenweg) ridge to Uetliberg (~2 hrs) with the whole lake below you.
places.notes: Verified operating cable car; the classic pairing with Uetliberg via the ridge Planet Trail. Check the March–April 2026 maintenance closure before visiting. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: The only public cable car in canton Zurich, rising to Felsenegg (~800 m) in about 5 minutes for a ridge viewpoint over Zurich, the lake and the Alps – on clear days from Säntis to the Bernese Oberland.
places.goodToKnow: Runs daily, high-frequency (summer season roughly 08:05–21:50). NOTE: closed for maintenance 2 March–10 April 2026 (and again spring 2027). Best combined with the ridge hike to Uetliberg on a clear day; family-friendly. Restaurant at Felsenegg.

places.name: Lindt Home of Chocolate
places.area: Kilchberg (Lake Zurich shore, ~7 km south of Zurich)
places.near: From Zurich Hauptbahnhof take S-Bahn S8 or S24 (~15 min) to Kilchberg station, then a short walk or Bus 165/163 to Schokoladenplatz. Note Kilchberg is outside Zurich fare zone 110, add zone 150. By car ~15 min via the Thalwil-Rüschlikon exit; underground parking on site.
places.order: Book the timed 'Chocolate museum' single ticket for the self-guided multimedia tour ending at the giant fountain with free tastings; optionally add a hands-on chocolate-making course. Leave time for the huge Lindt shop and the café.
places.notes: A crowd-pleasing, all-weather half-day; the chocolate fountain is a genuine wow moment for kids and adults. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Interactive Swiss chocolate museum at Lindt's home site, famous for the world's largest chocolate fountain (about 9 m tall, ~1,500 kg of flowing chocolate), plus the biggest Lindt shop (500 m²) and tastings.
places.goodToKnow: Very popular, book a timed slot online in advance and arrive within your 30-minute window. Allow ~1.5-2 hours for the tour plus shop. Kid-friendly and fully indoor (ideal on a rainy day). The fountain is the best photo spot. Tastings included with museum entry.

places.name: Swiss Science Center Technorama
places.near: Train from Zurich HB to Winterthur (~20-25 min), then Bus 5 (direction Technorama) or Bus 660 to the 'Technorama' stop, ~10 min. By car ~30 min via A1; free parking on site.
places.order: Standard day admission. Try the many hands-on stations, catch a live science show or lightning/electricity demonstration, and join a lab or workshop if available. Check the daily programme on arrival.
places.notes: The best rainy-day family attraction near Zurich for hands-on learning; genuinely engaging for adults too. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Switzerland's only large hands-on science center, with 500+ interactive discovery stations covering physics, chemistry and biology, plus live shows (e.g. high-voltage lightning), demonstrations and experiment labs.
places.goodToKnow: Open daily 10:00-17:00, 365 days/year. Allow 3-4+ hours, it is huge and very hands-on. Excellent for curious kids of all ages and fully indoor. Summer 2026 promo (1 Jul-31 Aug): up to 50% off public transport and 20% off admission. Time your visit around show schedules.

places.name: Alpamare
places.area: Pfäffikon SZ (on Lake Zurich, ~30 km / 30 min from Zurich)
places.near: Train from Zurich HB to Pfäffikon SZ (~30-40 min), then ~10-min walk or local bus to the Seedamm-Center. By car via A3, take the 'Seedamm-Center' exit; parking on site.
places.order: Buy a 4-hour or full-day ticket. Ride the big slides (e.g. the Cobra and speed slides), float the Rio Mare river, swim in the wave pool, and warm up in the 36°C brine thermal bath; there is a dedicated children's area for younger kids.
places.notes: The go-to family water park from a Zurich base; big-slide thrills plus toddler-friendly zones. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Switzerland's biggest water park: about 12 waterslides totaling ~2,100 m, an indoor wave pool, the Rio Mare lazy river, iodine-brine thermal baths and a wellness/sauna area.
places.goodToKnow: Open year-round and mostly indoor, so it works in any weather. Tickets from ~CHF 46 (4h) / ~CHF 49 (day); can be busy on weekends and holidays, so go early. Bring swimwear and towels (rentals available). Allow at least half a day. Minimum-height rules apply on some slides.

places.name: Bruno Weber Park
places.area: Dietikon (~15 km west of Zurich, access via Dietikon)
places.near: Train (S-Bahn) from Zurich HB to Dietikon (~15 min), then a scenic ~30-45 min signposted walk along the 'Bruno Weber path', or a short local bus/taxi. By car ~15-20 min from Zurich.
places.order: Simple day admission; wander the whole open-air art landscape, cross the water-garden bridges and let kids explore the giant creature sculptures. Great for photography.
places.notes: A quirky, magical off-the-beaten-path spot kids love; selected as the fun, photogenic 'hidden gem'. Check the limited open days before going. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: A fantastical 15,000 m² walk-through sculpture garden, Switzerland's largest single-artist sculpture park, filled with colorful surreal mythical creatures, dragons, gargoyle-like beasts, bridges, ponds and dreamlike architecture by artist Bruno Weber (1931-2011). A very Instagrammable hidden gem.
places.goodToKnow: Open only Wed, Sat and Sun 10:00-18:00 (until 17:00 Nov-Feb), so plan your day around those days. It is outdoor, best in dry weather. Admission ~CHF 15 adult, CHF 5 child (4-16), family (2+2) ~CHF 35, under 4 free. Allow 1-1.5 hours. Wear comfortable shoes; uneven paths and steps.

places.name: Zurich Tram Museum
places.near: Tram 11 or 15 to the 'Hedwigsteig' stop, or trams toward Rehalp; the museum is on Forchstrasse, ~15 min from the city center. Right on the tram network it celebrates.
places.order: Standard admission to explore the historic tram hall; let kids play conductor on the Cobralino children's tram. On select dates you can ride the vintage 'Museumslinie 21' historic tram through the city.
places.notes: A charming, inexpensive quirky spot for tram-loving kids; hands-on and indoors. Note the limited afternoon hours. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: A family-friendly museum with 15+ historic Zurich trams; kids can climb into old tram cars, see a tram from underneath, and 'drive' the children's tram 'Cobralino'.
places.goodToKnow: Open afternoons only, roughly Mon/Wed/Sat/Sun 13:00-18:00, so plan an afternoon visit. Admission ~CHF 14/9 adults, ~CHF 7 children (6-16), under 6 free. Allow 1-1.5 hours. Fully indoor, good rainy-day option. Small and low-key; best paired with another activity.

places.name: Rigi
places.area: Central Switzerland day trip (Rigi Kulm, above Lake Lucerne)
places.near: Fastest: SBB train Zurich HB to Arth-Goldau (~40 min), then the Rigi cogwheel railway to Rigi Kulm (~40 min). Scenic: train to Lucerne (~45 min), Lake Lucerne boat to Vitznau (~1 h), then cogwheel railway up. One way ~1.5-2 h from Zurich.
places.order: Consider the Rigi Day Pass covering all transport (train, cogwheel railways, cable car and, seasonally, the lake boat). Best route: cogwheel railway up to Rigi Kulm, easy panorama walks at the top, and a lake-steamer segment on the way. Family walking trails suit strollers in parts.
places.notes: Selected as the most family-friendly classic Alps day trip from Zurich: gentle, scenic and multi-modal (train + boat + cogwheel). · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: The 'Queen of the Mountains': a family-friendly summit (Rigi Kulm, 1,798 m) with panoramic views over Lake Lucerne and the Alps, reached by Europe's oldest cogwheel mountain railways, plus easy walking trails and the option to combine train, boat and cable car.
places.goodToKnow: Full-day trip, leave Zurich early. Bring layers, warm clothing and sturdy shoes even in summer, the summit is cool and can be cloudy, so pick a clear-forecast day for the views. The Rigi Day Pass (all 4 transport modes) is convenient for flexible family days. Easier and more relaxed than higher glacier peaks.

places.name: Titlis Cliff Walk
places.near: Hourly train Zurich HB to Lucerne (~45 min), then Zentralbahn train Lucerne to Engelberg (~45 min). From Engelberg take the TITLIS Xpress cable car to Stand, then the Rotair up to the summit (~30 min total). About 2 h plus cable cars each way.
places.order: Round-trip cable-car ticket from Engelberg to the summit. Ride the revolving Rotair, walk the Cliff Walk suspension bridge, enter the Glacier Cave, and play in the snow/Glacier Park at the top even in summer.
places.notes: Included as the second classic day trip for those wanting real glacier/snow at altitude; more of a big-ticket alpine outing than Rigi. (Confirm the 2026 Rotair-closure alternative when booking.) · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: A high-alpine glacier experience at 3,020 m: the TITLIS Rotair revolving cable car, year-round snow, a glacier cave, the Titlis Cliff Walk (Europe's highest suspension bridge) and big glacier/Alps panoramas, reachable from Zurich in under 2 hours plus cable cars.
places.goodToKnow: A full-day trip (nearly 4 hours in transit round trip), so start early. It is genuinely cold and snowy at the top year-round: bring warm clothes, gloves, sturdy shoes and sunglasses. Note the Rotair cable car is closed 17 Aug-11 Dec 2026, during which the summit is served by the new TITLIS Connect cable car instead. Pick a clear day for views.

places.name: Markthalle IM VIADUKT
places.near: Tram 4 or 13 to Dammweg, or S-Bahn/tram to Hardbrücke; a short walk along Viaduktstrasse. Central Zurich West location, easily combined with Freitag Tower and Frau Gerolds Garten.
places.order: Walk the length of the arches for the repeating-arch perspective shot, browse the design/fashion boutiques, then stop at the covered Markthalle for cheese, produce and coffee from local farmers.
places.notes: One of Zurich West's defining regeneration projects and a reliably photogenic, non-touristy stroll. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: A decommissioned 1894 stone railway viaduct whose 36+ arches now house independent design shops, artisan studios and a market hall (Markthalle) with regional food vendors - a signature Zurich West photo backdrop.
places.goodToKnow: Shops generally open daytime Mon-Sat (closed Sundays, though the outdoor arches and restaurants stay lively); Markthalle busiest on weekends. Fully pedestrian and family-friendly. Best light for the arches is late afternoon.

places.name: Freitag Tower
places.near: S-Bahn or tram to Hardbrücke, then a couple of minutes on foot; sits right beside the Hardbrücke bridge and next to Frau Gerolds Garten.
places.order: Climb the container stairways to the rooftop terrace for a free panorama of Zurich West, the Prime Tower and the rail yards; photograph the rust-red container stack from Geroldstrasse below for the iconic shot.
places.notes: Free, quick and genuinely Instagrammable - one of the easiest photo wins in Zurich West. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: A 26 m tower of 19 stacked rusty shipping containers (since 2006) housing the Freitag flagship store, topped by a free public viewing terrace over the ever-changing Zurich West skyline.
places.goodToKnow: Terrace access is free but only during store opening hours (typically daytime Mon-Sat, reduced/closed Sunday - check current hours). Great for architecture fans and families; go on a clear day for the best view.

places.name: Central Polybahn
places.near: Start at Central (tram hub next to the main station / Hauptbahnhof); the Polybahn lower station is right there. You can also walk down afterwards.
places.order: Ride the little red funicular up from Central, then walk out onto the Polyterrasse in front of the ETH main building for the classic postcard panorama of the Old Town and lake - a favourite romantic sunset spot.
places.notes: Best-value skyline view in central Zurich - short, historic and free at the top. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: A historic 1889 funicular (the 'Polybahnli') that climbs from Central square to the ETH Zurich Polyterrasse in about 100 seconds, delivering a free, sweeping viewpoint over the Old Town rooftops, the Limmat, Grossmunster/Fraumunster spires and Lake Zurich.
places.goodToKnow: Runs roughly every 2-5 minutes on weekdays/Saturdays; very cheap (a single ride, ZVV tickets accepted). The terrace itself is free and open anytime. Best at golden hour or dusk for skyline photos; great for couples and families.

places.name: Idaplatz
places.near: Tram 9 or 14 into Wiedikon, or S-Bahn to Zurich Wiedikon station, then a short walk; south-west of the centre.
places.order: Sit under the trees and soak up the neighbourhood rhythm; in April-May photograph the pink magnolia blossom around the square. A gentle detour away from the crowded Old Town.
places.notes: Included as a genuine local neighbourhood gem - lovely square atmosphere, best in magnolia season. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: A leafy, tree-shaded local square in trendy-but-authentic Wiedikon where residents (not tourists) linger - a charming hidden-gem plaza ringed by small cafes and international eateries, especially pretty when the magnolias bloom.
places.goodToKnow: Liveliest and prettiest in spring (magnolias) and on warm summer evenings. Relaxed, residential and family-friendly; a good 'live like a local' stop rather than a big sight.

places.name: Schipfe
places.area: Old Town (Altstadt / Lindenhof side), along the Limmat
places.near: Central Old Town - walk from Rennweg/Lindenhof or along Limmatquai; nearest trams stop at Rennweg or Rathaus. Best explored entirely on foot.
places.order: Stroll the cobbled riverside between Rathausbrucke (Town Hall Bridge) and Rudolf-Brun-Brucke, peek into the craft workshops and galleries, and shoot the old houses reflected in the Limmat with the far bank of the Old Town behind.
places.notes: A true hidden alley: central yet easily missed, and one of the Old Town's most romantic riverside spots. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: Zurich's oldest quarter - a pocket-sized riverside lane of medieval craftsmen's houses tucked below Lindenhof, still home to tiny artisan workshops and galleries, with romantic Limmat-front facades.
places.goodToKnow: Quiet, pedestrian-only and free; especially atmospheric in early morning or golden hour when the riverside facades catch the light. Workshops keep daytime hours. Compact - allow 20-30 minutes.

places.name: Bergstation Dolderbahn
places.near: Tram 3 or 8 to Romerhof, then the Dolderbahn (VBZ, ZVV tickets valid) up to Bergstation; runs daily approx. 06:20-23:30 every 10-20 min, roughly a 5-minute ride.
places.order: Ride the Dolderbahn up, take in the panorama over Zurich and the lake from the top station/Dolder area, then walk the well-marked Adlisberg forest trails or up to the Dolder Grand terrace for the view. A scenic escape above the city.
places.notes: A charming, locally-used funicular up the Zurichberg - scenic ride plus an elevated viewpoint over city and lake. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: A historic 1895 rack/funicular railway that climbs from Romerhof up the wooded Zurichberg to the Adlisberg, beside the Dolder recreation area and the landmark Dolder Grand hotel - the launch point for panoramic city, lake and (clear-day) Alps views.
places.goodToKnow: Covered by standard ZVV/city transport tickets. Best on a clear day for the Alps; combine with a forest walk or the Dolder ice rink/pool depending on season. Family-friendly and a pleasant, uncrowded viewpoint area.

places.name: James Joyce's Grave
places.near: Tram 5 or 6 to the Zoo terminus (Zurich Zoo / Fluntern); the cemetery is right by the zoo and FIFA headquarters on the edge of the woods.
places.order: Find the grave (site maps posted on the grounds) and the bronze statue, sit on the nearby bench to reflect, and enjoy the peaceful woodland setting; easy to pair with a Zoo visit or a Zurichberg walk.
places.notes: Well-regarded offbeat stop and genuine literary pilgrimage; conveniently next to the Zoo. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: The tranquil hillside grave of writer James Joyce (buried 1941, with wife Nora and son Giorgio nearby), marked by a contemplative bronze statue of Joyce seated with a cigar - a literary pilgrimage in a leafy, park-like cemetery next to Zurich Zoo.
places.goodToKnow: Free, no ticket; open cemetery hours (generally daytime, seasonal). Calm and respectful atmosphere - suits literature lovers and quiet reflection more than young children. Best on a clear, mild day.

places.name: Museum Mühlerama
places.near: Tram 2 or 4 or bus 33 toward Tiefenbrunnen, or S-Bahn S6/S16 to Tiefenbrunnen station, then a short walk to the Kulturareal Muhle Tiefenbrunnen.
places.order: Grind your cup of wheat through the historic mills, ride/see the old flour-sack slide, and (with the baking experience) mill, mix and take home your own warm loaf - a great family/rainy-day activity.
places.notes: Strong pick as a quirky small museum - genuinely interactive and one of Zurich's most family-friendly hidden gems. · v1 POI Finder
places.famousFor: A quirky, hands-on food-culture museum inside the century-old, still-operating Tiefenbrunnen industrial mill - visitors grind grain with historic tools (including a ~3,000-year-old stone) and can bake their own bread; a beloved former flour-sack slide delights kids.
places.goodToKnow: Open Tue-Sun (afternoons on weekdays, e.g. Tue/Thu/Fri/Sat 14:00-18:00, Wed 14:00-21:00, Sun 10:00-17:00; closed Mondays - verify current hours). Adults approx. CHF 15, children (6+) approx. CHF 9. Excellent for families; near the lake for a combined outing.

places.name: Masoala Rainforest Hall (Zoo Zürich)
places.near: Tram 6 from Zürich HB to terminus 'Zoo' (~20 min); by car ~15 min from centre, paid zoo car park at Zürichbergstrasse (outdoor, no height issue)
places.notes: zoo.ch opening-hours-prices page (fetched 2026-09)
places.famousFor: 11,000 m² walk-through Madagascar rainforest under one roof (lemurs, chameleons, flying foxes, 30 °C humidity) plus the Lewa Savanna with giraffes, rhinos and zebras side by side
places.goodToKnow: Open daily incl. Sunday: Oct zoo 9:00-18:00, Masoala 10:00-18:00 (Nov-Feb to 17:00). Adults CHF 32, 13-17 CHF 27, 6-12 CHF 18, under 6 free; family day pass 2 adults + own kids 6-17 CHF 85 (but 5 kids incl. 4-yr-old -> buy 2 adults + 3 paying kids ~CHF 132 vs family pass, check which is cheaper). Online tickets date-bound. Masoala has its own treetop walkway and Restaurant Masoala inside the hall. Allow 4-5 h for the whole zoo. · Kids: All ages; 4-yr-old loves lemurs

places.name: Sihlwald Wilderness Park & Forest Playground
places.area: Sihlwald / Langnau am Albis (~15 km S of Zürich)
places.near: S4 from Zürich HB to Sihlwald station (~25 min); by car Sihltalstrasse to Sihlwald, limited paid parking at the visitor centre
places.notes: wildnispark.ch/en/information (fetched 2026-09) + de.wikipedia Wildnispark Zürich for coords
places.famousFor: Switzerland's first nature discovery park: a wild, untouched beech forest along the Sihl with a big wilderness playground, covered picnic shelters, a forest adventure trail and a riverside visitor centre
places.goodToKnow: Forest, playground and shelters free and open 24/7 incl. Sundays; the Naturzentrum (exhibition/shop) is open until 26 Oct 2026 then closed for winter (27 Oct-28 Mar), so go early in your October week if you want the indoor part. Restaurant Sihlwald next to the centre. Combine with Langenberg wildlife park (same S4 line, 10 min apart). · Kids: Perfect 4-12; teens ok for hike

places.name: Wildnispark Zürich Langenberg
places.area: Langnau am Albis (~12 km S of Zürich)
places.near: S4 to Wildpark-Höfli (~20 min from HB) then 5 min walk; by car Albisstrasse, small paid car park at the entrance (fills on sunny weekends)
places.notes: wildnispark.ch visitor info + newinzurich.com 2025 + de.wikipedia Wildpark Langenberg (coords)
places.famousFor: Switzerland's oldest wildlife park (1869), 80 ha of forest with brown bears, wolves, lynx, elk, bison, wild boar and Przewalski horses in huge natural enclosures, and it is completely FREE
places.goodToKnow: Free entry, open daily incl. Sunday; east section 24/7, west section (bears/wolves side) and Wildcat House daily 8:00-19:00 Apr-Oct, 8:00-16:00 Nov-Mar; walk-in wild boar enclosure to 16:00. Restaurant Langenberg Mon-Fri 9-17, Sat-Sun 9-19. Bring the kids' bikes/scooter: wide forest roads. October = rutting season for red deer (loud stags). · Kids: All ages; stroller-ok paths

places.name: Jucker Farm Pumpkin Exhibition (Juckerhof Seegräben)
places.area: Seegräben, Pfäffikersee (~25 km E of Zürich)
places.near: S-Bahn to Aathal then 15-min uphill walk / bus; by car the farm is CAR-FREE - park at the TCS Gemeindeparkplatz Seegräben (5-min walk), very limited, farm strongly recommends public transport on weekends
places.notes: juckerfarm.ch Juckerhof page (fetched 2026-09, coords shown there) + newinzurich.com Sept 2026 + zuerioberland24
places.famousFor: Switzerland's most famous autumn outing: giant pumpkin sculptures on a lakeside farm (2026 theme 'Gute Reise' = travel/adventure), farm shop, pumpkin soup, petting goats, hay castle, tractor rides, apple maze
places.goodToKnow: Exhibition 19 Sep-25 Oct 2026, daily 9:00-17:00 incl. Sundays (later on Pumpkin Light Night dates). Entry CHF 11 weekdays / CHF 13 Sat-Sun, kids up to 12 FREE. Farm itself open 365 days (Oct 9:00-18:00). Go on a weekday morning with the van; weekends are crowded. Only 5 min from the Sauriermuseum Aathal - do both. · Kids: Ideal 4-12; teens for photos

places.name: Sauriermuseum Aathal (Dinosaur Museum)
places.near: S14 to Aathal, 600 m walk; by car right on Zürichstrasse (main Uster-Wetzikon road), FREE parking at the entrance and across the street (outdoor, no height limit)
places.notes: sauriermuseum.ch Besucherinformationen (fetched 2026-09) + en.wikipedia Aathal Dinosaur Museum (coords)
places.famousFor: Switzerland's dinosaur museum in a 1903 weaving mill: real skeletons the team dug up in Wyoming (Stegosaurus, Allosaurus, sauropods), Archaeopteryx casts, 645 exhibits over 4,500 m², a preparation lab you can watch, outdoor dino park
places.goodToKnow: Tue-Sat 10:00-17:00, Sun 10:00-18:00, CLOSED Monday. Adults CHF 22, kids 5-16 CHF 12, 4-yr-old CHF 6, family (parents + own kids 4-16) CHF 60 - the family ticket is a bargain for 7. Cafeteria + shop with fossils. Pair with Jucker Farm pumpkins (5 min away). · Kids: Dino-mad 4-12 heaven; teens ok

places.name: focusTerra Earthquake Simulator (ETH Zürich)
places.near: Polybahn from Central to ETH (1 min), then inside ETH main building; tram 6/9/10 to ETH/Universitätsspital
places.notes: focusterra.ethz.ch important-information + earthquake-simulator pages (web search 2026-09)
places.famousFor: ETH's free earth-science discovery centre: a walk-in earthquake simulator that shakes you through real quakes, glowing minerals, volcano and plate-tectonics exhibits - a hidden gem right next to the Polyterrasse
places.goodToKnow: FREE. Mon-Fri 9:00-17:00, Sat CLOSED, Sun 10:00-16:00. The earthquake simulator only runs inside a guided tour: free public tours SUNDAY at 11:00, 13:00 and 15:00, no booking needed (weekday tours are for pre-booked groups, 3 weeks ahead). Not for under-5s or pregnant women; 5-11 with an adult. Plan: Sunday morning Polybahn -> Polyterrasse photo -> 11:00 quake tour. · Kids: 5+ only on simulator; best 9-17

places.name: Beyer Clock and Watch Museum
places.near: Bahnhofstrasse 31, 3 min walk from Paradeplatz; tram to Paradeplatz or Rennweg
places.notes: beyer-ch.com museum + tickets pages (web search 2026-09) + en.wikipedia Beyer Watches & Jewellery (coords)
places.famousFor: One of the world's finest private watch collections (300 pieces from 1400 BC sundials to atomic clocks) in the basement of Beyer Chronometrie, Zürich's oldest watch house (1760), Rolex/Patek retailer upstairs
places.goodToKnow: Mon-Fri 14:00-18:00 only, closed Sat-Sun. Adults CHF 10 (incl. a glass of prosecco/orange juice), students CHF 5, kids to 12 free. IMPORTANT: museum stays open only until 30 Oct 2026, then closes to relocate (reopening elsewhere in Zürich mid-2027) - visit before then. Watch shopping upstairs; ask for the tax-free export form on purchases over CHF 300. · Kids: Short visit; teens + dad 30 min

places.name: Dolder Ice Rink (Kunsteisbahn Dolder)
places.near: Tram 3/8 to Römerhof, then the Dolderbahn rack railway to the top station, 4-min walk; by car paid parking on site at Dolder Eis & Bad (outdoor)
places.notes: doldereisundbad.ch ice-rink page (fetched 2026-09) + zuerich.com Dolder Eisbahn
places.famousFor: 1930s open-air rink above the city, 6,000 m² = one of Europe's largest outdoor ice surfaces, in the Dolder forest next to The Dolder Grand; skating, curling, ice-stock, weekend ice disco
places.goodToKnow: Season opens 17 Oct 2026 (to 7 Mar 2027) - so only useful if you are in Zürich from the 17th. Mon-Sat 9:00-22:30 (Wed to 20:00), Sun 9:00-17:45; may close early in warm/rainy weather. Adults 20+ CHF 8, kids 6+ CHF 4 (under 6 free), skate hire CHF 8. Bring gloves; helmets advised for the small ones. · Kids: All 5 kids; penguins aids for 4-yr

places.name: Hallenbad City (Indoor Pool)
places.near: 5-min walk from Bahnhofstrasse/Sihlporte; tram 2/9 to Sihlstrasse; Parkhaus Talgarten/Jelmoli nearby (check 2.0 m limits)
places.notes: stadt-zuerich.ch + zuerich.com Hallenbad City (web search 2026-09); coords de.wikipedia Hallenbad City
places.famousFor: Zürich's central 1941 indoor pool on the Schanzengraben moat: 50 m six-lane pool (28 °C), non-swimmer pool (30 °C), variable-depth pool, sauna - the rainy-day back-up in the city centre
places.goodToKnow: Daily 6:00-22:00 incl. Sunday. Cheap: adults CHF 8, youth CHF 6, kids CHF 4. Swim caps not required; swimwear rules strict (no cotton). Sauna is mixed except women-only Tue morning/Thu evening. · Kids: Kids' pool + 50 m pool; all ages

places.name: Limmat River Cruise (ZSG Limmatschiff)
places.near: Dock 'Zürich Landesmuseum' behind the Swiss National Museum, 3 min from HB; hop off at Bürkliplatz or Zürichhorn
places.notes: zuerich.com Limmat River Cruise page (fetched 2026-09) + zsg.ch timetable PDF
places.famousFor: Low flat-roofed boats that slip under the Old Town bridges from the National Museum down the Limmat and out to Zürichhorn - the cheapest sightseeing in Zürich and the best angle on Grossmünster/Fraumünster
places.goodToKnow: Runs April-October only (October = last weeks; winter timetable from 19 Oct 2026 - check zsg.ch). Adult CHF 4.60, kids 6-16 CHF 3.20, under 6 free; full round trip ~50 min, Landesmuseum-Zürichhorn ~25 min. Zürich Card and Swiss Travel Pass valid. WARNING: service is suspended whenever Limmat water level is too low/high - check zsg.ch traffic conditions the morning of. · Location needs verification · Kids: Easy 50 min; all ages

places.name: Planetenweg Uetliberg-Felsenegg (Planet Trail)
places.near: S10 from HB to Uetliberg (20 min), walk 10 min up to the start; finish at Felsenegg and take the Adliswil cable car down + S4 back. By car: park at Uetliberg is not possible (car-free), leave the van at Adliswil cable-car base and do it in reverse or go by train
places.notes: zuerich.com planet trail + swissfamilyfun.com + utokulm.ch (web search 2026-09); coords = Uto Kulm entry in his saved POI file
places.famousFor: A 1:1 billion scale model of the solar system along the Uetliberg ridge: start at the Sun by the summit, pass each planet (1 m = 1 million km) to Pluto at Felsenegg, ridge views of the lake and Alps the whole way
places.goodToKnow: Free, ~6 km, 1.5-2 h, wide gravel road with almost no climbing; big-wheel stroller works. October = golden beech forest + often above the fog (check webcam: if Zürich is grey, the ridge may be sunny). Restaurants at both ends (Uto Kulm, Felsenegg). Toboggan run at Uetliberg is winter-only, not October. · Kids: 6+ walk it; 4-yr in carrier/stroller
places.address: Uetliberg 652, 8143 Uetliberg (trail start near Uto Kulm)

places.name: Alter Botanischer Garten (Old Botanical Garden)
places.near: Entrances on Pelikanstrasse / Talstrasse; tram 2/9 to Sihlstrasse; walk from Paradeplatz 5 min
places.notes: bg.uzh.ch + zuerich.com (web search 2026-09); coords en.wikipedia Old Botanical Garden Zürich
places.famousFor: Hidden 1837 garden on the old 'zur Katz' bastion above the Schanzengraben moat: an 1851 octagonal palm house, Gessner herb garden, huge old trees and a hilltop terrace - a secret pocket 3 min from Bahnhofstrasse
places.goodToKnow: Free; Oct-Mar daily 8:00-18:00 (Apr-Sep 7:00-19:00). The Völkerkundemuseum (ethnographic museum, free) sits inside the garden. Good calm spot for a picnic between shopping stops. · Kids: Quiet 20-min stroll; playground nearby

places.name: Zürich Card (24h / 72h city pass)
places.area: Zürich city + zones 110-155 (incl. Uetliberg, Kilchberg, Zoo)
places.near: Buy at the Zürich Tourist Information in the main station hall, any SBB/ZVV ticket machine, or in the Zürich City Guide app
places.notes: zuerich.com Zürich Card Q&A (fetched 2026-09) + swissfamilyfun.com verdict
places.famousFor: All public transport (tram, bus, S-Bahn, Polybahn, Uetliberg train, short lake and Limmat boats) + free entry to most city museums (Landesmuseum, Kunsthaus collection, FIFA Museum, Rietberg) + discounts
places.goodToKnow: Adults CHF 29 (24h) / CHF 56 (72h); children 6-16 CHF 19 / CHF 37 (new prices from 13 Dec 2026). VERDICT for a family of 7 with a van: only worth it on a car-free museum day (e.g. Landesmuseum + FIFA + Kunsthaus + Polybahn + Limmat boat in 24h). Zoo Zürich and Lindt Home are NOT free (Lindt gives a discount only). If you just need trams, a 24h ZVV ticket is cheaper. · Location needs verification · Kids: Child card 6-16; under 6 free anyway

places.name: Schloss Rapperswil & Rose Gardens
places.area: Rapperswil-Jona, upper Lake Zurich (~30 km SE)
places.near: Car ~40 min via A3/Seedamm (park at Parkhaus Seedamm-Center or the lakeside P near the station - ask for van-suitable outdoor bays); train S7/S5 35 min from HB; or the ZSG 'Grosse Rundfahrt' boat from Bürkliplatz, ~2 h each way (runs until mid-Oct 2026)
places.notes: zuerich.com Rapperswil Castle + rapperswil-zuerichsee.ch (fetched 2026-09); htr.ch reopening; coords en.wikipedia Rapperswil Castle
places.famousFor: 13th-century castle on a rocky peninsula surrounded by the lake on three sides, reopened Nov 2024 after an 18-million-franc renovation with a new exhibition and tower viewpoint; free fallow-deer park on the north slope (since 1871), climbing wall and playground, and the 'town of roses' gardens below (15,000 roses, blooming until October)
places.goodToKnow: Castle & exhibition Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00, CLOSED Mon and 1 Nov; castle Buvette café Apr-Oct only (Tue-Fri 13-17, Sat-Sun 11-17). Deer park, rose gardens, Lindenhof hill and Capuchin monastery garden are free and always open. Stroller-accessible. Ticket prices via Visitor Center +41 55 225 77 00 (not published online). Do Rapperswil + Knies Kinderzoo + wooden bridge as one day. · Kids: Deer park + playground for 4-12

places.name: Knies Kinderzoo Rapperswil
places.near: Right next to Rapperswil station on Oberseestrasse; by car via Seedamm, zoo car park signed (outdoor)
places.notes: knieskinderzoo.ch + freizeit.ch prices 2026 (web search 2026-09); coords en.wikipedia Knie's Kinderzoo
places.famousFor: The Knie circus family's children's zoo (1962): elephants you can watch bathe in the Himmapan park, sea-lion shows, giraffes, camels, walk-in goat and pig petting areas, pony rides and a horse-drawn narrow-gauge tram - no predators, everything up close
places.goodToKnow: Season 1 Mar-1 Nov 2026, daily 9:00-18:00 incl. Sundays - so open all of October. Adults 16+ CHF 23, kids 4-15 CHF 9, under 4 free; family day ticket (2 parents + own kids) CHF 55 = clear winner for 7. Check the daily sea-lion show and elephant-bath times at the entrance. · Kids: Built for 2-12; teens 1 h max

places.name: Kloster Einsiedeln (Einsiedeln Abbey)
places.area: Einsiedeln, Canton Schwyz (~45 km S of Zürich)
places.near: Car ~50 min via A3 -> Pfäffikon SZ -> Einsiedeln (open-air parking on the Klosterplatz side / Parkplatz Brüel, no height issue); train S13/S40 via Wädenswil ~1 h
places.notes: kloster-einsiedeln.ch Öffnungszeiten + myswitzerland.com (fetched 2026-09); coords en.wikipedia Einsiedeln Abbey
places.famousFor: Switzerland's most important Baroque monastery and pilgrimage site (800,000 visitors a year): the Black Madonna in the Chapel of Grace, a jaw-dropping gilded church, the Rococo library, monks singing the Salve Regina daily, and a vast square with fountains framed by pre-Alpine hills
places.goodToKnow: Church free, daily 6:00-21:00 (Sun from 7:00; from All Saints to 20:30). Salve Regina sung ~16:30 daily (about 10 min, worth timing). Guided tour daily 14:00 except Sun/holidays, ~CHF 20, 1.5 h, no booking; 'Monkstrail' QR treasure hunt for kids (book ahead). Modest dress. The Bethlehem Diorama museum in town is only open by arrangement outside 27 Nov-6 Jan. Combine with Sattel-Hochstuckli or the drive on to Lucerne. · Kids: Quiet visit 30 min; big square to run

places.name: Rhyfall Mändli Boat Tours & Schlössli Wörth (Rhine Falls north bank)
places.area: Neuhausen am Rheinfall (~50 km N of Zürich)
places.near: Car ~45 min via A4 to Neuhausen; official Rheinfall car parks P1-P6 (cars up to 2.90 m CHF 5 first hour + CHF 2/h, so the van is fine); train to Neuhausen Rheinfall then 10 min walk down
places.notes: rhyfall-maendli.ch tickets + rock-tour pages, rheinfall.ch parking list (fetched 2026-09)
places.famousFor: The FREE side of Europe's largest waterfall: the Schlössli Wörth islet promenade at water level and the yellow Rhyfall Mändli boats - the 'Rock Experience' lands you on the mid-river rock to climb its stairs inside the spray
places.goodToKnow: Wörth-side access to the basin is FREE (the Laufen castle side charges CHF 5 / kids CHF 3.50). Boats run daily April-1 Nov: to 18 Oct 9:30-17:00, 19 Oct-1 Nov 11:00-17:00. Rock Experience CHF 22.50 (30 min, not for kids under 1.2 m, book online), 15-min family round trip CHF 10.50, 30-min audio round trip CHF 11, ferry across to Schloss Laufen CHF 6 (every 15 min, no booking). Under 6 free without a seat. Adventure Park Rheinfall ropes course is on the same bank. · Kids: Rock tour 1.2 m+; ferry all ages

places.name: Adventure Park Rheinfall (Ropes Course)
places.area: Neuhausen am Rheinfall, above the falls
places.near: Nohlstrasse, 5 min uphill from the Rheinfall P3/P4 car parks on the Neuhausen side; signed 'Adventure Park'
places.notes: ap-rheinfall.ch preise + oeffnungszeiten pages (fetched 2026-09)
places.famousFor: Switzerland's largest ropes park set in the forest right above the Rhine Falls: 12+ courses from yellow kids' trails to black expert lines, zip-lines with waterfall views, 3 h of climbing per ticket
places.goodToKnow: Oct 1-18 daily 10:00-19:00, last entry 16:30; from 20 Oct weekdays only for booked groups, weekends normal; season ends 2 Nov. Prices: adults 16+ CHF 41, 14-15 CHF 32.50, 10-13 CHF 26.50, 8-9 CHF 22.50 (adult must climb along, max 3 kids per adult), Kidsparcours 4-7 CHF 16.50 (2 h). Family 3+ incl. a parent = 10% off. Closed in storms - check the daily status posted by 8:00. Closed-toe shoes, hair tied. · Kids: Kids course 4-7; big courses 8+

places.name: GLOBUS
places.order: Latest fashion & largest shoe department in Switzerland, ground-floor Luxury Boulevard brands, beauty across six levels, design homeware (Alessi, Vitra, Bodum), and DELICATESSA Food & Wine
places.notes: Saved POI
places.famousFor: Landmark Swiss luxury department store on Bahnhofstrasse, Switzerland's leading department store (since 1892)
places.goodToKnow: High-end; six floors on Bahnhofstrasse; basement Delicatessa is a top gourmet address; steps from Zürich main station

places.name: Teddy's Souvenir Shop AG
places.order: Victorinox Swiss Army knives, watches, cuckoo clocks, cowbells, music boxes, hats, fridge magnets, soft toys
places.notes: Saved POI
places.famousFor: Long-established Swiss souvenir shop on Limmatquai in Zurich's old town
places.goodToKnow: On Limmatquai 34 (not Bahnhofstrasse); open daily including Sundays; classic central tourist-souvenir stop

places.name: Augustinergasse
places.near: Old Town (Altstadt), off Bahnhofstrasse near St. Peter
places.order: Small independent shops, Swiss souvenirs and handmade crafts; admire the historic facades
places.notes: Saved POI
places.famousFor: Charming medieval Old Town lane with colorful houses and carved wooden oriel windows
places.goodToKnow: Quiet, picturesque pedestrian lane; quick to walk; great for photos

places.name: Bahnhofstrasse
places.order: Window-shop luxury brands, watches and jewellery, visit Swiss chocolate shops, walk down to Lake Zurich at the end
places.notes: Saved POI
places.famousFor: Zurich's premier luxury shopping boulevard running from the main station to Lake Zurich, one of the world's most exclusive and expensive shopping streets
places.goodToKnow: Tram-served, largely traffic-calmed; high-end. Festive lights in winter

places.name: Jelmoli (closed 2025 - Manor returns 2027)
places.near: Bahnhofstrasse x Seidengasse, 5 min from HB
places.notes: swissinfo.ch + iamexpat.ch closure reports, finews.com Holmes Place 2026, tagesanzeiger/SRF Manor-to-Jelmoli 2027 (web search 2026-09); coords en.wikipedia Jelmoli
places.famousFor: Switzerland's oldest department store (1833), the 'glass palace' - CLOSED for good on 28 Feb 2025 after 192 years; the building is being gutted and rebuilt until end-2027 when Manor opens 13,000 m² on three floors plus rooftop restaurants
places.goodToKnow: STATUS OCT 2026: no shopping here - construction hoarding only (Holmes Place gym opens a temporary club in 2026). Don't route the family here; Globus (already on your list) is now the only classic department store on Bahnhofstrasse. Manor's city presence until 2027 is just the food/basics store in ShopVille at the main station. · Kids: N/A - building site in 2026

places.name: Victorinox Flagship Store Zürich
places.near: Rennweg 58, 2 min from Bahnhofstrasse; tram 6/7/11/13 to Rennweg
places.notes: victorinox.com flagship page + zuerich.com + Tripadvisor (web search 2026-09)
places.famousFor: The Swiss Army Knife brand's two-floor flagship on Rennweg: full knife, watch, luggage and cutlery range, and an on-the-spot engraving station to personalise each child's knife (the 'My First Victorinox' has a rounded tip)
places.goodToKnow: Mon-Fri 10:00-20:00, Sat 9:30-18:30, CLOSED Sunday. Engraving is cheap and done while you wait (name in Arabic letters may not be possible - Latin only, ask). Pack knives in checked luggage for the flight home. Purchases over CHF 300 qualify for the 8.1% VAT refund form. · Kids: Kids' knives + free engraving hit

places.name: Läderach Chocolatier Bahnhofstrasse
places.near: Bahnhofstrasse 106, right at the Bahnhofplatz end, 1 min from HB; smaller branch inside ShopVille (open Sundays)
places.notes: Yelp/bahnhofstrasse-zuerich.ch member page + laderach.com locations (web search 2026-09)
places.famousFor: Läderach's biggest Zürich store: the FrischSchoggi wall of fresh chocolate slabs broken to order (hazelnut, pistachio, strawberry, caramel-fleur-de-sel), pralines, and giant gift boxes - the chocolate stop closest to the station
places.goodToKnow: Mon-Sat 9:00-20:00, CLOSED Sunday (use the ShopVille branch on Sunday). Slabs sold by weight, ~CHF 8-12 per 100 g; they seal boxes for travel. Note Läderach faced boycott headlines in 2023-24 over the founder's family views - some UAE travellers prefer Sprüngli/Teuscher; your call. · Kids: Kids pick slabs; sampling

places.name: Schweizer Heimatwerk (Swiss Crafts Store)
places.near: Uraniastrasse 1 at the Rudolf-Brun bridge over the Limmat; tram 4/15 to Rudolf-Brun-Brücke; 5 min from HB
places.notes: zuerich.com Schweizer Heimatwerk + Yelp/Tripadvisor (web search 2026-09)
places.famousFor: 90-year-old cooperative selling only Swiss-made craft: wooden toys and spinning tops, hand-blown glass, linen, cowbells, paper-cut art, jewellery, cuckoo-free tasteful souvenirs - the anti-tourist-trap gift shop
places.goodToKnow: Mon-Sat 10:00-18:00, CLOSED Sunday. Second small branch inside the main station (ShopVille, open daily). Prices are high but everything is genuinely made in Switzerland; good for the 'gift for grandparents' run. · Kids: Wooden toys, music boxes

places.name: Schwarzenbach Kolonialwaren
places.near: Münstergasse 17/19, behind the Grossmünster in the Old Town; tram to Rathaus
places.notes: schwarzenbach.ch/en (fetched 2026-09) + zuerich.com
places.famousFor: Zürich's most photogenic old grocer (family-run since 1864, in Münstergasse since 1910): wooden drawers of spices, own-roasted coffee, 350+ bean-to-bar chocolates, dried fruit and nuts - with a little espresso/chocolate bar next door
places.goodToKnow: Mon-Fri 9:00-18:30, Sat 9:00-17:00, CLOSED Sunday. Great edible gifts (dates, apricots, spice mixes, chocolate) that survive the flight; staff bag things beautifully. Photo-friendly shopfront. · Kids: Dried-fruit & chocolate counter

places.name: Bucherer Bahnhofstrasse (Watches, tax-free)
places.near: Bahnhofstrasse 50, steps from Paradeplatz tram stop
places.notes: bucherer.com locations + estv.admin.ch tax-free-for-tourists + globalblue.com Switzerland (web search 2026-09)
places.famousFor: Switzerland's biggest watch & jewellery retailer (1888): multi-floor flagship with Rolex, Tudor, Patek, Chopard, Longines, Carl F. Bucherer - the one-stop for a serious watch purchase with export paperwork done in-house
places.goodToKnow: Mon-Sat, closed Sunday. TAX-FREE TIP: Swiss VAT is 8.1%; foreign residents get it refunded on purchases over CHF 300 per shop per day - ask for the export/Tax Free form, goods must leave CH within 30 days, get the form stamped at Zürich Airport customs (before check-in if the watch is in hold luggage) then refund at the Global Blue desk. Bring passport to the shop. UAE customs duty applies on arrival above the personal allowance. · Kids: Adults only really; 20 min

places.name: ShopVille Zürich Hauptbahnhof (Sunday shopping)
places.near: Under Zürich HB; escalators from the main hall and Bahnhofstrasse; van in Parkhaus Zürich HB / Sihlquai (check 2.0 m height at Parkhaus Hauptbahnhof)
places.notes: zuerich.com Sunday shopping page (fetched 2026-09) + sbb.ch ShopVille opening times; coords en.wikipedia ShopVille
places.famousFor: ~190 shops on three underground levels of the station that are open 365 days a year - the ONLY big Sunday shopping in the city: Migros and Coop supermarkets, Manor food, Läderach, Sprüngli, pharmacies, Müller (toys), fashion, SIM cards, bakeries
places.goodToKnow: Weekends/Sunday 9:00-20:00, weekdays most shops to 21:00 (supermarkets longer). Everything else on Bahnhofstrasse is CLOSED on Sundays - plan the Sunday for the zoo, a day trip or the lake and do groceries here. Also open daily: Stadelhofen station (35 shops) and Zürich Airport (80 shops, 6-21). · Kids: Toys at Müller, Migros snacks

places.name: Europaallee
places.near: Walk out the west (Sihlpost) exit of HB and you are on Lagerstrasse; Parkhaus Europaallee (underground, check 2.0 m before entering the van)
places.notes: europaallee.ch retail + zuerich.com Europaallee + Yelp passage hours (web search 2026-09); coords en.wikipedia Europaallee
places.famousFor: Zürich's newest quarter (finished 2020) beside the station tracks: flagship stores (Nike, Zara Home, Snipes, Bershka, Sportsline), the Europaallee Passage, Google's HQ, bakeries and burger bars along a pedestrian boulevard - the teens' shopping street
places.goodToKnow: Shops Mon-Sat roughly 10:00-20:00, CLOSED Sunday (the Passage too) - restaurants open Sunday. Bean Bank Coffee's big Europaallee branch is here. Seasonal 'Season Market' pop-ups in autumn. Good base for the 17- and 15-year-olds while parents do Bahnhofstrasse. · Kids: Teens' street-wear; playground

places.name: Sihlcity
places.area: Wiedikon / Brunau (Kreis 3), 2 km S of centre
places.near: S-Bahn to Zürich Saalsporthalle or tram 5/13 to Sihlcity Nord; by car straight off the A3 Brunau exit, Parkhaus Sihlcity 850 spaces, MAX HEIGHT 2.30 m - the 9-seat van fits
places.notes: sihlcity.ch Öffnungszeiten + minicity pages (fetched 2026-09), parkinglist.de height 2.30 m; coords en.wikipedia Sihlcity
places.famousFor: Zürich's big in-city mall (2007) in a former paper mill: ~80 shops incl. H&M, Zara, Coop, Migros, Interdiscount, a 9-screen Arena cinema, 'Minicity' supervised kids' play zone, Der Wilde Kaiser and 20+ restaurants, a hotel and wellness
places.goodToKnow: Shops Mon-Sat 9:00-20:00, CLOSED Sunday except a few special Sundays (11-18); mall corridors and cinema open daily, garage 24/7 via the Büttenweg night entrance. Minicity (ages 3-8, drop-off) Mon-Sat 10:00-18:30, last entry 17:45 - handy for the 4-year-old while the big ones shop. Rainy-day fallback. · Kids: Minicity play area 3-8; cinema

places.name: Glattzentrum (Einkaufszentrum Glatt)
places.area: Wallisellen, 8 km NE of Zürich near the airport
places.near: Car 15 min from centre or 10 min from the airport via A1/A51 (Wallisellen exit); Glattalbahn tram 12 from the airport / tram 11 from Bellevue to 'Glattzentrum'
places.notes: glatt.ch/en/service (fetched 2026-09) + parking.ch Glattzentrum Ost; coords en.wikipedia Glattzentrum
places.famousFor: Switzerland's highest-turnover mall (1975, US-style): 100+ shops on three levels - Manor, Globus, Coop, Migros, Apple reseller, Zara, H&M, Jack Wolfskin, Franz Carl Weber-style toy sections, big food court - with 4,500 FREE parking spaces
places.goodToKnow: Mon-Sat 9:00-20:00, CLOSED Sunday (rare special Sundays listed on glatt.ch). Parking free but max 4 h/day (video-monitored); multi-storey decks - the height limit is not published, use the open-air/ground-level areas or the Parkhaus Ost (municipal, 24/7) with the van. Best 'everything under one roof' stop on the way to/from the airport. · Kids: Big toy/kids floors; 2-3 h

places.name: Orell Füssli The Bookshop (English books)
places.near: Füsslistrasse 4, 1 min off Bahnhofstrasse between Paradeplatz and Rennweg
places.notes: orellfuessli.ch The Bookshop + newinzurich.com + inyourpocket (web search 2026-09)
places.famousFor: Zürich's largest English-language bookshop, now on the 3rd floor of the Orell Füssli Kramhof store: 40,000 English titles, a strong children's and YA section, board games, magazines, American candy, Starbucks attached
places.goodToKnow: Mon-Sat store hours (typically to 20:00), CLOSED Sunday. Free kids' story readings the first Saturday of the month. Good rainy-hour stop and for road-trip books for the 9- and 12-year-old. · Kids: Big English kids' floor; readings

places.name: Flohmarkt Bürkliplatz (Saturday Flea Market)
places.near: Tram 2/5/8/9/11 to Bürkliplatz; boat pier next door
places.notes: buerkli-flohmarkt.ch + zuerich.com flea market page (web search 2026-09); coords = Bürkliplatz entry in his POI file
places.famousFor: Zürich's classic Saturday flea market on the lake square: 150+ stalls of antiques, vintage watches, Swiss Army knives, vinyl, old cameras, coins, toys and curiosities, professional dealers alongside locals - with the Alps behind
places.goodToKnow: Every Saturday 2 May-31 Oct 2026, 7:00-17:00 - your October Saturdays are the last of the season. Cash (CHF) preferred, haggle politely. Combine with a ZSG short lake cruise from the same square. · Kids: Treasure hunt; watch the wallets

places.name: Rosenhof Market (Niederdorf craft market)
places.near: Rosenhof off Niederdorfstrasse / Marktgasse; tram to Rathaus or Rudolf-Brun-Brücke
places.notes: zuerich.com Rosenhof Market + myswitzerland events (web search 2026-09)
places.famousFor: Cosy courtyard market in the Old Town: Swiss handicrafts, handmade jewellery and pottery, leather, gemstones, ethnic objects and delicacies - the artisan alternative to souvenir shops
places.goodToKnow: Saturdays 10:00-18:00 from 7 Mar to 7 Nov 2026 (some years also Thursday afternoons - check rosenhof-markt.ch). Small - 30 min while walking the Niederdorf. · Kids: Handmade toys, jewellery for teens

places.name: Rechtswissenschaftliche Bibliothek
places.near: Rämistrasse 74/76, central Zürich near the University/ETH; tram to Kantonsschule or a short walk from the old town.
places.order: Looking straight up the open atrium at the curved tiers of railings converging toward the glass dome; the elliptical balconies are the signature shot.
places.notes: Saved POI
places.famousFor: Law Library of the University of Zürich (RWI), a Santiago Calatrava interior with stacked oval galleries under an elongated glass dome that appears to float on just eight points.
places.goodToKnow: Working academic library, free to enter during opening hours; be quiet and discreet with photos. Best light midday when the dome glows; closed weekends/holidays.

places.name: Polyterrasse (ETH Panorama Terrace)
places.near: Polybahn from Central (3 min, covered by Zürich Card/ZVV ticket) or tram 6/9/10 to ETH/Universitätsspital; 9 min walk uphill from HB
places.notes: zuerich.com Polyterrasse page (fetched 2026-09) + polybahn.ch hours
places.famousFor: The classic postcard of Zürich: the whole Old Town, both Münster towers, the Limmat and the lake to the Alps from the terrace in front of ETH's main building; golden at sunset, and the little red Polybahn arrives right onto it
places.goodToKnow: Free, open 24/7; best light late afternoon (sun behind you) and blue hour. Polybahn runs Mon-Fri ~6:45-19:15, Sat to ~14:00, NOT on Sundays - walk up via Leonhardstrasse on Sunday. Combine with focusTerra (Sun tours) and the Rechtswissenschaftliche Bibliothek atrium 5 min away. · Kids: Steps to run, wide safe terrace

places.name: Karlsturm Viewpoint (Grossmünster tower top)
places.near: Entrance inside the Grossmünster cloister side; tram 4/15 to Helmhaus
places.notes: departly.co.uk + daytripsfromzurich.com + myswitzerland Grossmünster (web search 2026-09); coords = Grossmünster entry in his POI file
places.famousFor: The best 360° over Zürich's roofs: Fraumünster spire, Lindenhof, Limmat bridges, the lake and Uetliberg from the open platform of the south tower, 187 steps up narrow spiral stairs
places.goodToKnow: Tower Apr-Oct 10:00-17:00 (last climb ~16:30), Nov-Mar to 16:30; CHF 5, combined with the Reformation museum CHF 10; closed in bad weather. Church itself free. NOTE: the Grossmünster is being renovated in 2026-27 with some areas restricted - confirm on the day that the tower is open. Sunday: opens after the morning service. · Kids: 187 steps: 6+; not for 4-yr

places.name: Quaibrücke Sunset Viewpoint
places.near: Tram 2/5/8/9/11 to Bürkliplatz or Bellevue; walk the south pavement
places.notes: en.wikipedia Quaibrücke, Zurich (coords + history)
